# Lens index

One line per lens. To read one in full, open `entries/<id>.md`. To start from a kind of project, open `kinds/<kind>.md`. How to think in the interview: [THINKING.md](THINKING.md). How to frame a project's conventions: [METHODOLOGIES.md](METHODOLOGIES.md).

Flags: **C** contested (offer it as a choice, with both sides) · **A** agents do this readily · **T** has a one-file tell · **E** has a pseudo-code example.

Axes in brackets: ⊕ the lens's primary effect, the reason to reach for it · + also helps · − costs. Laws name the axes they bear on. See [AXES.md](AXES.md).

`{kinds}`: where it matters most. `langs:` which languages have notes. `→` related lenses.

## Overlapping lenses

- `dry`, `duplicate-code`, `copy-and-paste-programming`, `wrong-abstraction`: Start from dry: it says what counts, duplicated knowledge rather than duplicated text. duplicate-code is how it shows in code, copy-and-paste-programming is the habit that produces it, and wrong-abstraction is what an eager merge of copies that only look alike produces.
- `yagni`, `speculative-generality`, `over-engineering`: yagni is the principle. speculative-generality is the symptom inside a class or module (hooks, parameters and abstractions nothing uses), and over-engineering is the same thing at system scale.
- `dead-code`, `lava-flow`: dead-code is the code that does nothing. lava-flow is why it stays: nobody dares remove it. Use lava-flow when the question is history and ownership, dead-code when it is the code itself.
- `law-of-demeter`, `message-chains`, `middle-man`: law-of-demeter is the principle, message-chains is how a break shows, and middle-man is what over-applying it produces. Read all three before recommending either direction.
- `god-object`, `large-class`, `interface-bloat`: god-object is the design failure (one class owns too much of the control), large-class the visible symptom, and interface-bloat the failure seen from the clients that depend on it.
- `cargo-cult-programming`, `golden-hammer`, `dogma-over-pragma`: All four are practice without reasons. cargo-cult-programming is the code-level form, blind-pattern-following the architecture and process form, golden-hammer one tool used for everything, and dogma-over-pragma a rule kept where its reason doesn't apply.
- `big-ball-of-mud`, `spaghetti-code`: big-ball-of-mud is the whole system; spaghetti-code is tangled control flow inside a module. A codebase can have either without the other.
- `mock-everything`, `fragile-test`, `assertion-free-test`: mock-everything is over-mocking until a test checks nothing real, assertion-free-test is a test that checks nothing at all, and fragile-test is the symptom both often produce: tests that break on refactors that change no behaviour.
- `kiss`, `occams-razor`: kiss is the one to use for code. occams-razor is the general form, for choosing between explanations, such as when debugging.
- `global-state`, `singleton`: global-state is the problem. singleton is one way to produce it, and the pattern entry covers when a single instance is still right.
- `switch-statements`, `state`, `strategy`, `open-closed-principle`: switch-statements is the smell, and state and strategy are the two usual remedies: state when the switch is on an object's lifecycle, strategy when it chooses an algorithm. Exhaustive matching on a closed set is often better than either. open-closed-principle says when the switch is worth replacing at all: when others add cases, not when you own every one.
- `anemic-domain-model`, `data-class`, `domain-model`, `transaction-script`: Decide domain-model or transaction-script first: it is a choice per subdomain, not a ranking. Only then is anemic-domain-model a fault, when rich rules were wanted and ended up in services. data-class is the smell on one class, and is fine on boundary types.
- `repository`, `generic-repository`, `data-mapper`, `active-record`: active-record or data-mapper is the persistence choice. repository sits on a data mapper and speaks the domain's language; generic-repository is a repository that just re-exposes the ORM.
- `ports-and-adapters`, `dependency-rule`, `dependency-inversion-principle`, `layered-architecture`: dependency-rule is the principle (dependencies point toward policy). dependency-inversion-principle is the same idea at the scale of one dependency: the interface belongs to the code that needs it, which is how a single import is made to point inward. ports-and-adapters is the architecture built on both, and layered-architecture the older style it corrects, where the domain depends on persistence.
- `postels-law`, `tolerant-reader`: postels-law is the general (and contested) principle; tolerant-reader is the narrow, safe version: a consumer reads only the fields it needs and ignores the rest, while still rejecting what breaks the contract.
- `hyrums-law`, `breaking-change-surface`, `semantic-versioning-discipline`, `deprecation-policy`: hyrums-law explains why every observable behaviour is API. breaking-change-surface lists those surfaces, semantic-versioning-discipline says how to signal changes to them, and deprecation-policy how to retire them.
- `test-double-taxonomy`, `mock-everything`, `fake-over-mock`: test-double-taxonomy gives the words. mock-everything is the failure (mocking until nothing real is tested), and fake-over-mock the contested preference for in-memory fakes of owned stateful collaborators.
- `golden-master-test`, `fragile-test`: golden-master-test is right when the output is the contract. fragile-test is what snapshots of incidental output turn into.
- `validate-at-the-boundary`, `parse-dont-validate`, `trusting-client-input`: validate-at-the-boundary says where checks belong, parse-dont-validate how to make them stick (turn input into a type that can't be invalid), and trusting-client-input is the failure of checking only on the client.
- `secure-by-default`, `fail-open-vs-fail-closed`, `least-privilege`: secure-by-default and least-privilege set what is allowed without asking. fail-open-vs-fail-closed is the separate decision of what happens when a check itself fails; tooling and security often answer it differently.
- `swallowed-errors`, `error-handling-policy`, `exceptions-for-control-flow`: Start from error-handling-policy, which decides how errors travel in this codebase. swallowed-errors and exceptions-for-control-flow are the two common ways code breaks that policy.
- `single-responsibility-principle`, `divergent-change`, `shotgun-surgery`: single-responsibility-principle is the principle: one reason to change per module. divergent-change is the smell when it is broken one way (one module changes for many reasons), shotgun-surgery when it is broken the other way (one reason to change touches many modules). Use the smells to find it in code.
- `interface-segregation-principle`, `interface-bloat`: interface-segregation-principle is the principle seen from the caller (depend only on what you use); interface-bloat is the type that broke it. Start from the principle when reviewing a function's parameters, from interface-bloat when reviewing the type itself.

## Principles

- [`dependency-rule`](entries/dependency-rule.md) **The Dependency Rule** · principle/architecture [TE] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {web-api,fullstack-web,mobile,desktop} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Source code dependencies point inward, toward policy. Business rules never import the database, the web framework or the UI; those outer parts depend on the rules, and where control has to flow outward the inner code defines an interface for the outer code to implement. → `ports-and-adapters` `layered-architecture` `solid` `law-of-leaky-abstractions`
- [`least-privilege`](entries/least-privilege.md) **Least privilege** · principle/security [E] (security⊕ delivery− operability−) {iac,serverless,platforms,plugin-host,distributed} langs:rs,ts: Give every user, process, service account, token and plugin only the permissions its job needs, for only as long as it needs them, so a mistake or a compromise can do only that much harm. → `secure-by-default` `defense-in-depth` `broken-object-level-authorization` `hard-coded-secrets`
- [`secure-by-default`](entries/secure-by-default.md) **Secure by default** · principle/security [TE] (security⊕ delivery−) {library-sdk,plugin-host,cli-devtool,platforms,iac} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: The out-of-the-box setting is the safe one, and anything dangerous (network access, disabled TLS checks, open CORS, debug mode, running untrusted code) must be switched on explicitly, by a setting whose name says it is dangerous. → `least-privilege` `defense-in-depth` `principle-of-least-astonishment` `hyrums-law` `ssrf`
- [`defense-in-depth`](entries/defense-in-depth.md) **Defense in depth** · principle/security [E] (security⊕ delivery− runtime− change_cost−) {platforms,web-api,distributed,fullstack-web}: Protect anything that matters with several independent layers of control, so one missed check, bug or misconfiguration doesn't expose it on its own. → `least-privilege` `secure-by-default` `validate-at-the-boundary` `broken-object-level-authorization` `shotgun-surgery`
- [`fail-fast`](entries/fail-fast.md) **Fail Fast** · principle/design [E] (reliability⊕ operability+) {cli-devtool,web-api,data-pipeline,library-sdk,serverless} langs:py,java,cs,go,rs,ts: Detect a bad state as early as possible and stop right there with a clear error, instead of carrying on and failing later in a place that hides the cause. → `swallowed-errors` `error-handling-policy` `fail-open-vs-fail-closed` `murphys-law`
- [`make-illegal-states-unrepresentable`](entries/make-illegal-states-unrepresentable.md) **Make Illegal States Unrepresentable** · principle/design [TE] (reliability⊕ change_cost+ delivery−) {web-frontend,fullstack-web,tui,compilers-tooling,library-sdk,web-api} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Shape your types so that combinations of data that can't happen in the domain can't be built at all. Usually this means a closed set of variants (a sum type or discriminated union), each carrying only the fields that make sense for it, instead of one record with a status flag and a pile of optional fields. → `parse-dont-validate` `primitive-obsession` `temporary-field` `switch-statements` `state` `data-clumps`
- [`tell-dont-ask`](entries/tell-dont-ask.md) **Tell, Don't Ask** · principle/design [CE] (change_cost⊕ reliability+) langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Rather than asking an object for its data and deciding for it, tell the object what you want and let it decide using its own data. It puts behaviour next to the data it uses. → `law-of-demeter` `feature-envy` `data-class` `message-chains` `command-query-separation` `inappropriate-intimacy`
- [`command-query-separation`](entries/command-query-separation.md) **Command-Query Separation (CQS)** · principle/design [TE] (change_cost⊕ reliability+) {library-sdk,plugin-host} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Every method should either change state (a command) or return an answer (a query), not both. Then queries can be called freely, in any order and as often as you like, and changes happen only where a command is called. → `principle-of-least-astonishment` `fluent-interface` `tell-dont-ask` `functional-core-imperative-shell` `immutability-by-default`
- [`composition-over-inheritance`](entries/composition-over-inheritance.md) **Composition over Inheritance** · principle/design [E] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {library-sdk,plugin-host,games} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Get reuse and variation by giving an object other objects to delegate to, rather than by subclassing. Inheritance ties a subclass to its parent's internals; composition lets you combine and swap parts, including at runtime. → `refused-bequest` `parallel-inheritance-hierarchies` `strategy` `decorator` `template-method` `liskov-substitution-principle`
- [`solid`](entries/solid.md) **SOLID** · principle/design [C] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) langs:py,go: Robert C. Martin's name for five object-oriented design principles, each an entry of its own here: single responsibility, open/closed, Liskov substitution, interface segregation and dependency inversion. Use this entry when a project names SOLID as a whole; judge code against the five. → `single-responsibility-principle` `open-closed-principle` `liskov-substitution-principle` `interface-segregation-principle` `dependency-inversion-principle` `yagni`
- [`single-responsibility-principle`](entries/single-responsibility-principle.md) **Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)** · principle/design [CE] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {web-api,fullstack-web,web-frontend} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go: A module should have one reason to change, meaning it answers to one group of people or one concern. Code that changes for different reasons, at different times, belongs in different modules. → `solid` `divergent-change` `large-class` `god-object` `shotgun-surgery`
- [`open-closed-principle`](entries/open-closed-principle.md) **Open/Closed Principle (OCP)** · principle/design [CE] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {plugin-host,library-sdk,compilers-tooling} langs:py,ts,java,rs,go: Code that others build on should be open to extension and closed to modification. Adding a new case (a payment method, a file format, an output) should mean adding code at an extension point, not editing the code that already works. → `solid` `switch-statements` `speculative-generality` `strategy` `microkernel` `yagni`
- [`liskov-substitution-principle`](entries/liskov-substitution-principle.md) **Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP)** · principle/design [TE] (reliability⊕ change_cost+ delivery−) {plugin-host,library-sdk,plugins-extensions} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Any implementation of a type must work wherever the type is expected, without callers knowing which one they got. A subtype may accept more and promise more, never require more or promise less, and must keep the type's invariants. → `solid` `refused-bequest` `composition-over-inheritance` `contract-test` `principle-of-least-astonishment`
- [`interface-segregation-principle`](entries/interface-segregation-principle.md) **Interface Segregation Principle (ISP)** · principle/design [E] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {library-sdk,plugin-host} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go: No client should depend on methods it doesn't use. Shape interfaces around what each caller needs, so a change to one capability doesn't ripple into code that never touched it, and an implementation never has to fake the parts it can't do. → `solid` `interface-bloat` `liskov-substitution-principle` `refused-bequest` `mock-everything`
- [`dependency-inversion-principle`](entries/dependency-inversion-principle.md) **Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)** · principle/design [CE] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {web-api,fullstack-web,library-sdk} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go: High-level policy should not depend on low-level details; both should depend on abstractions, and the abstraction belongs to the policy side. The business code says what it needs (a way to store an order), and the database code implements that. → `solid` `dependency-rule` `ports-and-adapters` `dependency-injection` `infrastructure-ignorance`
- [`tenant-isolation`](entries/tenant-isolation.md) **Tenant isolation** · principle/security [E] (security⊕ delivery−) {web-api,fullstack-web,platforms,serverless,databases-storage} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go: In a system that serves several customers from shared code and storage, every query, cache key, file path, queue message and background job carries the tenant it belongs to, and the tenant comes from the verified identity, so one tenant's data can't reach another by any path. → `broken-object-level-authorization` `defense-in-depth` `secure-by-default` `least-privilege` `global-state` `generic-repository` `contract-test`
- [`idempotency`](entries/idempotency.md) **Idempotency** · principle/architecture [E] (reliability⊕ operability+ runtime− delivery−) {web-api,distributed,event-driven,serverless,data-pipeline} langs:py,ts,java,cs: Design operations so that doing one twice has the same effect as doing it once, because networks, clients, queues and schedulers will repeat it: idempotent HTTP methods, idempotency keys for POST, and consumers that recognise a message they have already handled. → `outbox` `saga` `fallacies-of-distributed-computing` `pipes-and-filters` `circuit-breaker` `command-query-separation`
- [`dry`](entries/dry.md) **DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself)** · principle/design [E] (change_cost⊕ reliability+) {iac}: Each piece of knowledge, such as a business rule, constant or config value, should live in exactly one authoritative place. It is about knowledge, not text: two identical lines that encode different decisions are not duplication. → `kiss` `yagni` `wrong-abstraction`
- [`kiss`](entries/kiss.md) **KISS (Keep It Simple, Stupid)** · principle/design [E] (change_cost⊕ delivery+): Pick the simplest design that meets the actual requirement. → `yagni` `galls-law` `kernighans-law` `dry`
- [`law-of-demeter`](entries/law-of-demeter.md) **Law of Demeter** · principle/design [CE] (change_cost⊕) {fullstack-web}: A unit should only talk to its direct collaborators, not reach through them to their internals; also called the principle of least knowledge or "don't talk to strangers". → `law-of-leaky-abstractions`
- [`occams-razor`](entries/occams-razor.md) **Occam's Razor** · principle/decisions [E] (change_cost⊕ operability+ delivery+) {distributed,serverless}: Among options that do the job, prefer the one with the fewest moving parts and assumptions, in design and in debugging. → `kiss` `yagni` `teslers-law`
- [`postels-law`](entries/postels-law.md) **Postel's Law** · principle/quality [CE] (reliability⊕ security− change_cost−) {web-api,compilers-tooling,data-pipeline,event-driven,plugin-host}: Be strict in what you send and tolerant in what you accept. Also called the Robustness Principle. → `murphys-law` `principle-of-least-astonishment`
- [`premature-optimization`](entries/premature-optimization.md) **Premature Optimization** · principle/planning [CE] (change_cost⊕ delivery+) {games,embedded,scientific,databases-storage}: Don't make code faster before you know it is a bottleneck; write it clearly, measure, then optimise the hot spots. Also called Knuth's optimization principle. → `pareto-principle` `yagni`
- [`principle-of-least-astonishment`](entries/principle-of-least-astonishment.md) **Principle of Least Astonishment** · principle/design [TE] (change_cost⊕ reliability+) {library-sdk,cli-devtool,web-api,plugins-extensions,tui,plugin-host}: Code and APIs should do what a reader would guess from how they look and from the habits of the codebase around them. Also called the Rule of Least Surprise. → `postels-law`
- [`yagni`](entries/yagni.md) **YAGNI** · principle/design [E] (delivery⊕ change_cost+) {library-sdk,plugins-extensions}: Don't build features, options or abstractions until something actually needs them. Short for "You Aren't Gonna Need It". → `occams-razor` `second-system-effect` `premature-optimization` `solid`

## Practices

- [`validate-at-the-boundary`](entries/validate-at-the-boundary.md) **Validate at the boundary** · practice/security [E] (security⊕ reliability⊕ change_cost+ delivery−) {web-api,cli-devtool,data-pipeline,library-sdk,plugin-host,event-driven} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Check data where it enters from a less trusted place (a request, a file, a queue, a CLI argument, a third-party API), against an allow-list of what is acceptable, and reject the rest there, so the code inside can rely on what it receives. → `parse-dont-validate` `trusting-client-input` `injection` `postels-law` `primitive-obsession` `defense-in-depth`
- [`error-handling-policy`](entries/error-handling-policy.md) **Error Handling Policy** · practice/design [TE] (reliability⊕ change_cost+ operability+ delivery−) {library-sdk,cli-devtool,web-api,plugin-host,platforms} langs:go,rs,java,cs,py,ts: Decide once, for the whole codebase, how errors are represented (values, exceptions or panics), which ones may abort the program, and at which layer each kind is handled, so every module fails the same way. → `fail-fast` `swallowed-errors` `exceptions-for-control-flow` `inconsistent-error-contract` `fail-open-vs-fail-closed`
- [`fail-open-vs-fail-closed`](entries/fail-open-vs-fail-closed.md) **Fail Open vs Fail Closed** · practice/design [E] (security⊕ reliability⊕ delivery−) {cli-devtool,plugin-host,plugins-extensions,web-api,distributed,platforms} langs:go,py,ts: For each place where a check or a dependency can fail, decide on purpose whether failure lets things through (fail open) or stops them (fail closed), and make the code do that; the anti-pattern is leaving it to whatever the error path happens to do. → `fail-fast` `swallowed-errors` `error-handling-policy` `postels-law` `murphys-law`
- [`semantic-versioning-discipline`](entries/semantic-versioning-discipline.md) **Semantic Versioning Discipline** · practice/api [C] (change_cost⊕ reliability+ delivery−) {library-sdk,cli-devtool,plugin-host,platforms,iac} langs:rs,ts,py,go,java,cs: Declare what your public API is, then let every release number say what changed in it, a major bump for a break, a minor for an addition or deprecation, a patch for a compatible fix, and actually hold to that. → `breaking-change-surface` `deprecation-policy` `hyrums-law` `non-exhaustive-types`
- [`deprecation-policy`](entries/deprecation-policy.md) **Deprecation Policy** · practice/api [E] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {library-sdk,web-api,cli-devtool,plugin-host,platforms,iac} langs:py,java,cs,rs,ts,go: Remove public things in stages, marking them deprecated with a replacement and a removal date or version, warning users, and only deleting after a stated window, so users can migrate on their own schedule. → `semantic-versioning-discipline` `breaking-change-surface` `hyrums-law` `lava-flow`
- [`breaking-change-surface`](entries/breaking-change-surface.md) **Breaking-Change Surface** · practice/api [E] (change_cost⊕ reliability+ delivery−) {library-sdk,cli-devtool,plugin-host,web-api,platforms,iac} langs:ts,py,go,rs,java,cs: Know every surface outsiders depend on, not just function signatures but CLI flags and output, exit codes, error messages, config schema, file formats, wire formats and defaults, and treat changes to any of them as API changes. → `hyrums-law` `semantic-versioning-discipline` `deprecation-policy` `non-exhaustive-types` `postels-law` `inconsistent-error-contract`
- [`non-exhaustive-types`](entries/non-exhaustive-types.md) **Non-Exhaustive Types** · practice/api [CE] (change_cost⊕ reliability−) {library-sdk,plugin-host,web-api,platforms} langs:rs,java,cs,ts,go,py: When a public enum, struct or interface is likely to grow, mark it so outside code can't depend on knowing every case or field, so you can add a variant, field or method later without a breaking release. → `breaking-change-surface` `semantic-versioning-discipline` `hyrums-law` `postels-law`
- [`contract-test`](entries/contract-test.md) **Contract Test** · practice/testing [E] (reliability⊕ change_cost+ delivery−) {plugin-host,library-sdk,distributed,event-driven,web-api,databases-storage} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: A test suite that pins what one side of an interface promises the other, and runs against every party that claims to keep the promise. One form is consumer-driven contracts, where the consumers of a service write down what they rely on and the provider runs those checks. Another is a contract suite that a host or library ships so every plugin, adapter or backend can prove it behaves as the host expects. → `test-double-taxonomy` `fake-over-mock` `liskov-substitution-principle` `hyrums-law` `postels-law` `testing-pyramid`
- [`property-based-test`](entries/property-based-test.md) **Property-Based Test** · practice/testing [E] (reliability⊕ delivery−) {compilers-tooling,library-sdk,databases-storage,scientific,data-pipeline} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Instead of a few hand-picked examples, state a rule that must hold for every input (the output is sorted, decoding undoes encoding, the parts add up to the total), let a library generate many inputs, and when one fails, let it shrink that input to the smallest case that still fails. → `golden-master-test` `test-data-builder` `parse-dont-validate`
- [`fake-over-mock`](entries/fake-over-mock.md) **Prefer Fakes over Mocks** · practice/testing [CE] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {web-api,fullstack-web,databases-storage,event-driven} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: For a stateful collaborator you own, such as a repository, cache or queue, write one small in-memory fake that behaves like the real thing and use it across tests, instead of configuring a mock with expected calls in each test. Tests then check the resulting state rather than the calls made. → `mock-everything` `test-double-taxonomy` `contract-test` `fragile-test`
- [`parse-dont-validate`](entries/parse-dont-validate.md) **Parse, Don't Validate** · practice/design [TE] (reliability⊕ security+ change_cost+ delivery−) {web-api,cli-devtool,library-sdk,data-pipeline,plugin-host} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: At the edge of the system, turn raw input into a type that can only hold valid values, and pass that type inward. A check that returns true or false and then hands on the raw value forgets what it learned, so the same checks get repeated, or skipped, deeper in. → `make-illegal-states-unrepresentable` `primitive-obsession` `postels-law` `functional-core-imperative-shell`
- [`functional-core-imperative-shell`](entries/functional-core-imperative-shell.md) **Functional Core, Imperative Shell** · practice/design [E] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {cli-devtool,tui,games,web-api,data-pipeline,event-driven} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Put the decisions in pure functions that take values and return values, and keep a thin outer layer that reads input, calls the core, and carries out the effects it returns. The core is tested with plain values and no doubles; the shell is kept simple enough to need only a few integration tests. → `hard-to-test-code` `mock-everything` `global-state` `command-query-separation` `immutability-by-default` `parse-dont-validate`
- [`immutability-by-default`](entries/immutability-by-default.md) **Immutability by Default** · practice/design [E] (reliability⊕ change_cost+ runtime−) {web-frontend,fullstack-web,distributed,library-sdk,data-pipeline} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Make values, records and collections unchangeable unless there is a reason for them to change, and produce a modified copy instead of editing in place. Mutation is then rare and visible, so shared data can't be changed behind a reader's back. → `global-state` `functional-core-imperative-shell` `make-illegal-states-unrepresentable` `command-query-separation`
- [`authorize-before-side-effects`](entries/authorize-before-side-effects.md) **Authorize before side effects** · practice/security [E] (security⊕ reliability+) {web-api,fullstack-web,platforms,plugin-host,serverless} langs:py,ts,java,cs: Decide whether the caller may do the thing before doing any part of it: no file write, delete, email, payment, outbound call or cache change happens until the permission check has passed. → `broken-object-level-authorization` `least-privilege` `fail-fast` `defense-in-depth` `fail-open-vs-fail-closed` `saga`
- [`unauthenticated-vs-forbidden`](entries/unauthenticated-vs-forbidden.md) **401 Unauthorized versus 403 Forbidden** · practice/api [E] (reliability⊕ operability+) {web-api,fullstack-web,mobile,library-sdk} langs:py,ts,java,cs: Answer 401 when the server doesn't know who the caller is (no credentials, or invalid or expired ones), with a WWW-Authenticate challenge, and 403 when it knows who they are and the answer is still no, because clients act differently on each: 401 means sign in again, 403 means don't retry. → `inconsistent-error-contract` `broken-object-level-authorization` `user-enumeration` `hyrums-law` `principle-of-least-astonishment`
- [`additive-features`](entries/additive-features.md) **Additive Features** · practice/api [TE] (change_cost⊕ reliability+ delivery−) {library-sdk,embedded,plugin-host,compilers-tooling} langs:rs,go,py,ts,cs,cpp: A build-time feature or conditional-compilation flag should only add to a public API, never remove or change what is already there, because a dependency graph turns on the union of every flag that anyone in it asked for. → `breaking-change-surface` `semantic-versioning-discipline` `non-exhaustive-types` `hyrums-law`
- [`versioned-plugin-protocol`](entries/versioned-plugin-protocol.md) **Versioned Plugin Protocol** · practice/api [E] (change_cost⊕ operability+ reliability+ delivery−) {plugin-host,plugins-extensions,cli-devtool,compilers-tooling,platforms} langs:rs,go,py,ts: Give a plugin or extension protocol its own version number, separate from the release of the host that speaks it, and have host and plugin state which protocol versions they speak, so the host can ship releases freely and an incompatible pair fails clearly at load time. → `microkernel` `semantic-versioning-discipline` `breaking-change-surface` `tolerant-reader` `deprecation-policy` `contract-test`
- [`ui-thread-confinement`](entries/ui-thread-confinement.md) **UI thread confinement** · practice/design [TE] (reliability⊕ runtime⊕ delivery−) {tui,desktop,mobile,web-frontend,games} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: UI state and widgets are touched only from the one thread or event loop that owns them, and anything slow or blocking (network, disk, heavy computation, waiting) runs elsewhere and hands its result back to that thread as a message or posted task. → `observer` `model-view-update` `functional-core-imperative-shell` `immutability-by-default` `global-state` `resource-leak`
- [`boy-scout-rule`](entries/boy-scout-rule.md) **The Boy Scout Rule** · practice/quality (change_cost⊕ delivery−): Leave the code a little cleaner than you found it each time you touch it. → `broken-windows-theory` `technical-debt`
- [`technical-debt`](entries/technical-debt.md) **Technical Debt** · practice/quality [T] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {fullstack-web,platforms}: Shortcuts in code buy speed now and charge interest later as extra effort on every change, until the debt is paid down. → `lehmans-laws` `pareto-principle`
- [`testing-pyramid`](entries/testing-pyramid.md) **Testing Pyramid** · practice/quality [CE] (change_cost⊕ delivery+) {web-frontend,fullstack-web,mobile,web-api}: Put most of your tests at the cheap, fast unit level, a smaller layer of integration tests above that, and just a handful of slow end-to-end tests at the top. Also called the test pyramid. → `pesticide-paradox`

## Laws

- [`amdahls-law`](entries/amdahls-law.md) **Amdahl's Law** · law/scale [E] (bears on runtime) {distributed,data-pipeline,scientific,ml-training,databases-storage}: The part of the work that has to run in sequence caps how much faster you can get by adding parallel workers. → `gustafsons-law`
- [`broken-windows-theory`](entries/broken-windows-theory.md) **Broken Windows Theory** · law/quality [TE] (bears on change_cost, reliability): Small signs of neglect left unfixed tell everyone that quality doesn't matter here, so the mess grows; also called software entropy. → `boy-scout-rule` `technical-debt`
- [`cap-theorem`](entries/cap-theorem.md) **CAP Theorem** · law/architecture [E] (bears on reliability) {distributed,databases-storage}: When a network partition splits a distributed data store, it has to choose between staying consistent and staying available; also called Brewer's theorem. → `fallacies-of-distributed-computing`
- [`fallacies-of-distributed-computing`](entries/fallacies-of-distributed-computing.md) **Fallacies of Distributed Computing** · law/architecture [TE] (bears on reliability, security, runtime) {distributed,web-api,event-driven,serverless,mobile} langs:py: Eight false assumptions about networks, such as that they are reliable, fast, secure and unchanging, that lead to fragile distributed systems. → `cap-theorem` `law-of-leaky-abstractions`
- [`galls-law`](entries/galls-law.md) **Gall's Law** · law/architecture (bears on delivery, reliability) {distributed,platforms,plugins-extensions}: Complex systems that work grew out of simple systems that worked; designing one from scratch rarely does. → `kiss` `yagni` `second-system-effect`
- [`gustafsons-law`](entries/gustafsons-law.md) **Gustafson's Law** · law/scale [E] (bears on runtime) {distributed,data-pipeline,scientific,ml-training}: If the problem grows with the hardware, parallel speedup can stay close to linear, because the serial part stays roughly fixed while the parallel part grows. → `amdahls-law`
- [`hyrums-law`](entries/hyrums-law.md) **Hyrum's Law** · law/architecture [E] (bears on change_cost, reliability) {library-sdk,web-api,platforms,plugins-extensions,cli-devtool,plugin-host}: With enough users, every observable behaviour of an API ends up depended on by someone, whatever the docs promise. → `law-of-leaky-abstractions` `postels-law`
- [`kernighans-law`](entries/kernighans-law.md) **Kernighan's Law** · law/quality [TE] (bears on change_cost, reliability): Debugging is twice as hard as writing code, so code written as cleverly as you can manage is code you can't debug. → `kiss`
- [`law-of-leaky-abstractions`](entries/law-of-leaky-abstractions.md) **The Law of Leaky Abstractions** · law/architecture [E] (bears on runtime, reliability, change_cost) {fullstack-web,databases-storage,library-sdk,iac,plugin-host}: Every non-trivial abstraction lets some of the underlying details through, so you still need to understand what it hides. → `fallacies-of-distributed-computing` `hyrums-law` `law-of-demeter`
- [`law-of-unintended-consequences`](entries/law-of-unintended-consequences.md) **Law of Unintended Consequences** · law/architecture (bears on reliability, change_cost) {platforms,distributed,iac}: Any real change to a complex system will have effects nobody planned for, good, bad, or the opposite of what was meant. → `hyrums-law` `murphys-law`
- [`lehmans-laws`](entries/lehmans-laws.md) **Lehman's Laws of Software Evolution** · law/quality (bears on change_cost) {fullstack-web,platforms,desktop}: A system used in the real world has to keep changing to stay useful, and each change adds complexity unless someone works to remove it. → `technical-debt` `zawinskis-law`
- [`lindy-effect`](entries/lindy-effect.md) **Lindy Effect** · law/decisions (bears on change_cost, reliability) {web-frontend,embedded}: The longer a technology has already been in use, the longer it is likely to stay in use, which favours proven, "boring" choices. → `occams-razor`
- [`murphys-law`](entries/murphys-law.md) **Murphy's Law** · law/quality [E] (bears on reliability) {embedded,data-pipeline,event-driven,mobile}: Anything that can go wrong eventually will, so handle the failure cases instead of assuming them away. Also called Sod's Law. → `law-of-unintended-consequences` `postels-law`
- [`pareto-principle`](entries/pareto-principle.md) **Pareto Principle** · law/decisions (bears on runtime, reliability) {games,scientific}: A small share of causes produces most of the effect, so find the vital few (hot code, crashing bugs, used features) and spend effort there. Also called the 80/20 rule. → `premature-optimization`
- [`pesticide-paradox`](entries/pesticide-paradox.md) **Pesticide Paradox** · law/quality [E] (bears on reliability) {compilers-tooling,databases-storage,library-sdk}: Running the same tests over and over finds fewer and fewer new bugs, so the suite has to grow and change with the code. → `testing-pyramid`
- [`second-system-effect`](entries/second-system-effect.md) **Second-System Effect** · law/architecture (bears on delivery, change_cost) {platforms,library-sdk}: Once a lean first system has worked, the team tends to over-design the version that replaces it and pile in all the ideas they held back the first time. → `zawinskis-law` `yagni`
- [`teslers-law`](entries/teslers-law.md) **Tesler's Law** · law/architecture [E] (bears on change_cost, operability) {cli-devtool,library-sdk,web-api,iac}: Every task has some complexity that cannot be removed, only moved, so decide deliberately whether the user, the caller or the system carries it. Also called the Law of Conservation of Complexity. → `occams-razor` `principle-of-least-astonishment`
- [`zawinskis-law`](entries/zawinskis-law.md) **Zawinski's Law** · law/architecture (bears on change_cost) {cli-devtool,desktop,plugins-extensions}: Every program keeps growing features until it tries to do everything, even read mail, so scope has to be defended. → `second-system-effect` `lehmans-laws`
- [`littles-law`](entries/littles-law.md) **Little's Law** · law/scale [E] (bears on runtime, reliability) {web-api,distributed,databases-storage,data-pipeline,serverless}: In a stable system, the average number of items in it equals the average arrival rate times the average time each item spends inside (L = λW). Fix any two and the third follows. → `amdahls-law` `gustafsons-law` `premature-optimization` `circuit-breaker`

## Design patterns

- [`bounded-context`](entries/bounded-context.md) **Bounded Context** · pattern/architecture [TE] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {distributed,web-api,fullstack-web,platforms,event-driven} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Draw an explicit boundary around each model, in code, data and team ownership, and keep terms consistent inside it, accepting that the same word (customer, product, course) means different things in different contexts. → `ubiquitous-language` `context-map` `anti-corruption-layer` `core-subdomain` `shared-database` `distributed-monolith` `big-ball-of-mud` `drifting-terminology`
- [`ubiquitous-language`](entries/ubiquitous-language.md) **Ubiquitous Language** · pattern/design [E] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {web-api,fullstack-web,library-sdk,plugin-host}: Developers and domain experts share one vocabulary within a bounded context and use it everywhere, in talk, docs and especially code, so renaming a concept in conversation means renaming it in code too. → `drifting-terminology` `bounded-context` `domain-allergy` `principle-of-least-astonishment`
- [`context-map`](entries/context-map.md) **Context Map** · pattern/architecture (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {distributed,platforms,event-driven}: A map of the bounded contexts in play, including outside systems, and of how each pair relates (who is upstream, who translates, what is shared), drawn as things are now rather than as hoped. → `bounded-context` `anti-corruption-layer` `shared-database` `big-ball-of-mud`
- [`core-subdomain`](entries/core-subdomain.md) **Core, Supporting and Generic Subdomains** · pattern/architecture [E] (delivery⊕ change_cost+) {web-api,fullstack-web,platforms,distributed}: Sort the business areas a system covers into core (what sets the business apart), supporting (needed and specific, but no edge) and generic (solved problems), and spend design rigour on the core while keeping the rest simple or buying it. → `bounded-context` `reinventing-the-wheel` `over-engineering` `yagni` `domain-allergy` `aggregate`
- [`abstract-factory`](entries/abstract-factory.md) **Abstract Factory** · pattern/creational [E] (change_cost⊕ reliability+ delivery−) {desktop,mobile,library-sdk} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: One factory object creates a whole family of related objects, so the caller gets parts that fit together without naming their concrete classes. Sometimes called a kit. → `factory-method` `builder` `prototype` `bridge` `facade` `singleton`
- [`builder`](entries/builder.md) **Builder** · pattern/creational [TE] (change_cost⊕ reliability+ delivery−) {library-sdk,compilers-tooling} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: Build a complicated object in named steps through a separate builder, instead of one constructor with a long list of options. → `abstract-factory` `factory-method` `composite` `bridge`
- [`factory-method`](entries/factory-method.md) **Factory Method** · pattern/creational [E] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {library-sdk,plugins-extensions} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: A base class calls an overridable creation method, so subclasses decide which concrete class gets built. Also called a virtual constructor. → `abstract-factory` `template-method` `prototype` `builder`
- [`prototype`](entries/prototype.md) **Prototype** · pattern/creational [TE] (change_cost⊕ runtime+ reliability−) {games} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: Make new objects by copying a configured existing one, with the object itself doing the copying, so the caller needn't know its class. Also called clone. → `factory-method` `abstract-factory` `composite` `decorator` `memento` `command`
- [`singleton`](entries/singleton.md) **Singleton** · pattern/creational [CTE] (reliability⊕ runtime+ change_cost−) {mobile,games,embedded,desktop,serverless} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: A class allows only one instance of itself and hands out a global way to reach it. → `facade` `flyweight` `abstract-factory` `builder` `prototype` `global-state`
- [`adapter`](entries/adapter.md) **Adapter** · pattern/structural [E] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {library-sdk,plugins-extensions,web-api,data-pipeline} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: Wrap an object so it offers the interface the caller expects, translating calls and data on the way. Also called a wrapper. → `bridge` `decorator` `proxy` `facade`
- [`bridge`](entries/bridge.md) **Bridge** · pattern/structural [E] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {desktop,embedded,games} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: Split a class that varies along two independent axes into two hierarchies, the abstraction and its implementation, linked by composition. → `adapter` `strategy` `state` `abstract-factory` `builder`
- [`composite`](entries/composite.md) **Composite** · pattern/structural [E] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {web-frontend,desktop,compilers-tooling,games,tui} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: Leaves and containers share one interface, so code can treat a whole tree the same way it treats a single item. → `decorator` `iterator` `visitor` `builder` `flyweight` `chain-of-responsibility` `prototype`
- [`decorator`](entries/decorator.md) **Decorator** · pattern/structural [E] (change_cost⊕ operability−) {web-api,library-sdk} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: Add behaviour to an object by wrapping it in another object with the same interface, and stack wrappers instead of subclassing every combination. Also called a wrapper. → `adapter` `proxy` `composite` `chain-of-responsibility` `strategy` `prototype`
- [`facade`](entries/facade.md) **Facade** · pattern/structural [E] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {library-sdk,web-api,platforms,plugin-host} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: Give a complex subsystem one simple entry point that covers what callers actually need. → `adapter` `mediator` `proxy` `abstract-factory` `singleton` `flyweight` `god-object`
- [`flyweight`](entries/flyweight.md) **Flyweight** · pattern/structural [E] (runtime⊕ change_cost−) {games,embedded,compilers-tooling} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: Save memory by sharing the common, immutable part of many similar objects and keeping only the per-object part separate. → `composite` `singleton` `facade` `premature-optimization`
- [`proxy`](entries/proxy.md) **Proxy** · pattern/structural [E] (change_cost⊕ reliability−) {distributed,databases-storage,library-sdk} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: A stand-in with the same interface as the real object, which controls access to it (lazily creating it, checking permissions, caching, logging, or reaching it over a network). Also called a surrogate. → `decorator` `adapter` `facade` `flyweight`
- [`chain-of-responsibility`](entries/chain-of-responsibility.md) **Chain of Responsibility** · pattern/behavioral [TE] (change_cost⊕ reliability− operability−) {web-api,fullstack-web,event-driven,plugin-host} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: A request passes along a line of handlers, and each one either deals with it or hands it on to the next. Middleware that can stop a request is the everyday form; a pipeline where every stage transforms the data is Pipes and Filters, not this. → `decorator` `composite` `command` `mediator` `observer`
- [`command`](entries/command.md) **Command** · pattern/behavioral [E] (change_cost⊕ operability+ delivery−) {desktop,games,cli-devtool,event-driven,web-frontend,tui} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: Wrap a request in an object that carries everything needed to run it, so it can be passed around, queued, logged, retried or undone; also called Action or Transaction. → `memento` `strategy` `chain-of-responsibility` `visitor` `prototype`
- [`iterator`](entries/iterator.md) **Iterator** · pattern/behavioral [TE] (change_cost⊕ runtime+ reliability−) {databases-storage,data-pipeline,library-sdk} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: Walk the elements of a collection without exposing how it stores them, with each walk keeping its own position; also called Cursor. → `composite` `visitor` `factory-method` `memento`
- [`mediator`](entries/mediator.md) **Mediator** · pattern/behavioral [CTE] (change_cost⊕ operability−) {web-frontend,desktop,mobile,tui,web-api} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: Objects stop talking to each other directly and go through one coordinator that knows how they interact. Classically it coordinates UI components; in back ends the name now also covers an in-process dispatcher that routes each request or command to its one handler. → `observer` `facade` `chain-of-responsibility` `command` `god-object`
- [`memento`](entries/memento.md) **Memento** · pattern/behavioral [E] (change_cost⊕ reliability+ runtime−) {desktop,games,tui} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: An object produces an opaque snapshot of its own state that others can store and hand back for restoring, without seeing inside it; also called Snapshot. → `command` `iterator` `prototype`
- [`observer`](entries/observer.md) **Observer** · pattern/behavioral [TE] (change_cost⊕ reliability− operability−) {web-frontend,desktop,mobile,games,event-driven,tui,plugin-host} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: Interested objects subscribe to a publisher and get told when something happens, without the publisher knowing who they are; also called Publish-Subscribe, Listener or Event Subscriber. → `mediator` `chain-of-responsibility` `command`
- [`state`](entries/state.md) **State** · pattern/behavioral [TE] (change_cost⊕ reliability+ delivery−) {embedded,games,mobile,web-frontend,event-driven,tui} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: Move each state's behaviour into its own object and let the owner swap which one it delegates to, so it acts as if it changed class. → `strategy` `bridge` `adapter`
- [`strategy`](entries/strategy.md) **Strategy** · pattern/behavioral [TE] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {library-sdk,scientific,ml-training} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: Put each variant of an algorithm behind one interface and let the caller plug in the one it wants; also called Policy. → `state` `template-method` `command` `decorator` `bridge`
- [`template-method`](entries/template-method.md) **Template Method** · pattern/behavioral [TE] (change_cost⊕) {library-sdk,plugins-extensions,data-pipeline,plugin-host} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: A base class fixes the steps of an algorithm and subclasses fill in or override individual steps without changing the order. → `strategy` `factory-method`
- [`visitor`](entries/visitor.md) **Visitor** · pattern/behavioral [CTE] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {compilers-tooling,cli-devtool,plugin-host} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs,cpp: Keep operations in separate visitor objects that walk a structure of mixed element types, so new operations don't touch the element classes (double dispatch). → `composite` `iterator` `command`
- [`repository`](entries/repository.md) **Repository** · pattern/design [E] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {web-api,fullstack-web,databases-storage} langs:java,cs,py,ts,go,rs: Give the domain a collection-like interface for getting and storing its objects, so callers ask for "the overdue loans" and never see how the query is built or where the rows live. → `generic-repository` `data-mapper` `unit-of-work` `domain-model` `table-data-gateway` `facade` `over-engineering`
- [`service-layer`](entries/service-layer.md) **Service Layer** · pattern/architecture [E] (change_cost⊕ security+ reliability+ delivery−) {web-api,fullstack-web,event-driven} langs:java,cs,py,ts,go,rs: Define the application's operations in one layer that every entry point (HTTP, CLI, queue consumer) calls, so each use case coordinates transactions, authorisation and domain calls in one place. → `fat-controller` `anemic-domain-model` `transaction-script` `domain-model` `facade` `middle-man` `unit-of-work`
- [`transaction-script`](entries/transaction-script.md) **Transaction Script** · pattern/design [E] (delivery⊕ change_cost+) {web-api,cli-devtool,data-pipeline,serverless} langs:py,go: Organise business logic as one procedure per request or use case, which reads its data, applies the rules and writes the result, top to bottom. → `domain-model` `service-layer` `anemic-domain-model` `table-data-gateway` `duplicate-code` `shotgun-surgery` `kiss`
- [`domain-model`](entries/domain-model.md) **Domain Model** · pattern/design [E] (change_cost⊕ reliability+ delivery−) {web-api,fullstack-web,distributed} langs:java,cs,py,ts,go,rs: Model the business as objects that carry both their data and the rules about it, so invariants live with the state they protect instead of in the procedures that use it. → `anemic-domain-model` `transaction-script` `data-mapper` `repository` `active-record` `data-class` `feature-envy`
- [`active-record`](entries/active-record.md) **Active Record** · pattern/design [E] (delivery⊕ change_cost−) {fullstack-web,web-api} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Let each object wrap one database row and carry both its persistence (save, find, delete) and its domain logic, so the class and the table are the same shape. → `data-mapper` `domain-model` `table-data-gateway` `god-object` `large-class` `repository`
- [`data-mapper`](entries/data-mapper.md) **Data Mapper** · pattern/design [E] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {web-api,databases-storage} langs:java,cs,py,ts,go,rs: Move data between domain objects and the database with a separate mapping layer, so the domain objects know nothing about tables and the schema can differ from the object model. → `active-record` `repository` `unit-of-work` `identity-map` `domain-model` `law-of-leaky-abstractions`
- [`unit-of-work`](entries/unit-of-work.md) **Unit of Work** · pattern/design [E] (reliability⊕ runtime+ change_cost−) {web-api,databases-storage} langs:py,java,cs,ts,go,rs: Track every object a business operation loads, creates or changes, then write all the changes out together in one commit, so the operation succeeds or fails as a whole. → `identity-map` `repository` `data-mapper` `service-layer`
- [`table-data-gateway`](entries/table-data-gateway.md) **Table Data Gateway** · pattern/design [E] (change_cost⊕) {web-api,databases-storage,data-pipeline} langs:go,rs,java,cs,py,ts: Put all the SQL for one table behind one object with plain methods (find, insert, update by id), and hand back plain data, so the rest of the code never builds queries. Row Data Gateway is the per-row variant. → `active-record` `repository` `transaction-script` `data-mapper` `n-plus-one-queries`
- [`identity-map`](entries/identity-map.md) **Identity Map** · pattern/design [E] (reliability⊕ runtime+) {databases-storage} langs:py,cs,java,ts: Keep a map of every object loaded in the current operation, keyed by id, so loading the same record twice returns the same object instead of two copies that can disagree. → `unit-of-work` `data-mapper` `repository` `global-state`
- [`data-transfer-object`](entries/data-transfer-object.md) **Data Transfer Object** · pattern/architecture [E] (change_cost⊕ security+ runtime+ delivery−) {web-api,fullstack-web,distributed,library-sdk} langs:py,java,cs,ts,go,rs: Carry data across a boundary (a network call, an API, a queue) in a plain object shaped for that boundary, separate from the domain objects behind it. → `data-class` `data-mapper` `facade` `over-engineering` `shotgun-surgery`
- [`dependency-injection`](entries/dependency-injection.md) **Dependency Injection** · pattern/design [E] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {web-api,cli-devtool,library-sdk,plugin-host} langs:java,cs,py,ts,go,rs: Hand an object the collaborators it needs (usually through its constructor) instead of letting it create or look them up, and wire the whole graph in one place at startup, the composition root. → `singleton` `global-state` `hard-to-test-code` `mock-everything` `abstract-factory` `strategy` `solid`
- [`front-controller`](entries/front-controller.md) **Front Controller** · pattern/architecture [E] (change_cost⊕ security+ operability+) {web-api,fullstack-web} langs:java,cs,py,ts,go,rs: Route every request through one handler that runs the shared steps (auth, logging, error handling) and then dispatches to the specific handler; in today's frameworks this is the router plus its middleware pipeline. → `chain-of-responsibility` `decorator` `command` `fat-controller` `mediator`
- [`entity`](entries/entity.md) **Entity** · pattern/design [E] (reliability⊕ delivery−) {web-api,fullstack-web,databases-storage} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: A domain object defined by a lasting identity rather than by its attributes, so it stays the same thing while its data changes, and two with the same data can still be different things. → `value-object` `aggregate` `data-class` `primitive-obsession`
- [`value-object`](entries/value-object.md) **Value Object** · pattern/design [E] (reliability⊕ change_cost+ delivery−) {web-api,fullstack-web,library-sdk,scientific,data-pipeline} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: A small immutable object defined only by its attributes, with no identity, that carries the meaning and rules of a domain value such as an amount with its currency, a date range or a dose with its unit. → `primitive-obsession` `entity` `data-clumps` `over-engineering`
- [`aggregate`](entries/aggregate.md) **Aggregate** · pattern/design [E] (reliability⊕ runtime+ delivery−) {web-api,fullstack-web,distributed,event-driven} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: A cluster of entities and value objects treated as one unit for change, reached only through its root entity, which enforces the cluster's invariants; one transaction changes one aggregate, and other aggregates are updated afterwards. → `entity` `value-object` `domain-event` `factory-ddd` `bounded-context` `law-of-demeter` `over-engineering`
- [`domain-service`](entries/domain-service.md) **Domain Service** · pattern/design [E] (change_cost⊕) {web-api,fullstack-web} langs:go,rs,java,cs: A stateless operation named in the domain's language, for a significant piece of domain logic that doesn't naturally belong to any one entity or value object, typically because it involves several of them. → `entity` `aggregate` `business-logic-in-helpers` `feature-envy` `data-class`
- [`domain-event`](entries/domain-event.md) **Domain Event** · pattern/design [E] (change_cost⊕ operability− delivery−) {event-driven,distributed,web-api} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: An immutable record, named in the past tense, of something that happened in the domain that experts care about (ClaimApproved, PaymentFailed), raised by the model so other parts can react without the source knowing them. → `observer` `aggregate` `bounded-context` `anti-corruption-layer` `mediator`
- [`specification`](entries/specification.md) **Specification** · pattern/design [CE] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {web-api,fullstack-web} langs:cs,java,py,ts,go,rs: A business rule packaged as an object with one question, "is this candidate satisfied?", so the rule has a name, can be combined with and, or and not, and can be reused for validation, selection and building. → `strategy` `composite` `duplicate-code` `over-engineering`
- [`factory-ddd`](entries/factory-ddd.md) **Factory (DDD)** · pattern/design [E] (reliability⊕ change_cost+ delivery−) {web-api,fullstack-web} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: An object or method whose job is to create a whole aggregate, or a complex value object, in a valid state in one step, so callers don't assemble its parts and can't produce a half-built one. Not the GoF patterns abstract-factory or factory-method, which are about choosing which class to instantiate. → `abstract-factory` `factory-method` `builder` `aggregate` `value-object`
- [`anti-corruption-layer`](entries/anti-corruption-layer.md) **Anti-Corruption Layer** · pattern/architecture [TE] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {web-api,distributed,platforms,fullstack-web} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: A translating layer the downstream side owns, between its model and an external or legacy system, so the other system's concepts, codes and quirks don't leak into its own model. → `adapter` `facade` `bounded-context` `context-map` `big-ball-of-mud` `infrastructure-ignorance`
- [`ports-and-adapters`](entries/ports-and-adapters.md) **Ports and Adapters** · pattern/architecture [CE] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {web-api,fullstack-web,distributed,event-driven,plugin-host} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Keep the application core free of technology. It talks to the outside world only through ports, which are interfaces it defines, and each database, UI, queue or test harness plugs in through an adapter that translates to that port. → `dependency-rule` `layered-architecture` `adapter` `solid` `microkernel`
- [`layered-architecture`](entries/layered-architecture.md) **Layered Architecture** · pattern/architecture [E] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {web-api,fullstack-web,desktop} langs:java,cs,py,go: Split the application into horizontal layers, usually presentation, business (service), persistence and database, where each layer only calls the one below it. → `dependency-rule` `ports-and-adapters` `shotgun-surgery` `big-ball-of-mud`
- [`cqrs`](entries/cqrs.md) **CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation)** · pattern/architecture [CE] (change_cost⊕ runtime+ reliability− delivery−) {event-driven,distributed,web-api} langs:cs,java,py,ts: Use one model to change data (commands) and a separate model to read it (queries), so each can be shaped, stored and scaled for its own job. → `event-sourcing` `outbox` `saga` `yagni`
- [`event-sourcing`](entries/event-sourcing.md) **Event Sourcing** · pattern/architecture [CE] (operability⊕ change_cost− delivery−) {event-driven,distributed,databases-storage} langs:cs,java,ts,rs,py: Store every change as an immutable event in an append-only log and derive current state by replaying the events, instead of overwriting the current state in place. → `cqrs` `outbox` `saga` `memento`
- [`pipes-and-filters`](entries/pipes-and-filters.md) **Pipes and Filters** · pattern/architecture [E] (change_cost⊕ runtime+ reliability−) {data-pipeline,cli-devtool,compilers-tooling,ml-training,event-driven} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Break processing into a chain of independent steps (filters), each taking input and producing output, joined by pipes that carry data from one to the next and hold no logic of their own. → `chain-of-responsibility` `decorator` `functional-decomposition`
- [`microkernel`](entries/microkernel.md) **Microkernel (plugin architecture)** · pattern/architecture [E] (change_cost⊕ security− delivery−) {plugin-host,plugins-extensions,desktop,cli-devtool,compilers-tooling} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Keep a small core that provides the minimal shared machinery, and put features in plugins that the core discovers and calls through a stable, versioned contract. → `ports-and-adapters` `hyrums-law` `strategy` `switch-statements`
- [`tolerant-reader`](entries/tolerant-reader.md) **Tolerant Reader** · pattern/architecture [CE] (change_cost⊕ reliability+) {distributed,event-driven,web-api,library-sdk} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: When consuming another service's data, read only the fields you need, assume as little about the structure as you can, and ignore what you don't recognise, so the provider can add things without breaking you. → `postels-law` `hyrums-law` `adapter`
- [`strangler-fig`](entries/strangler-fig.md) **Strangler Fig** · pattern/architecture [E] (change_cost⊕ reliability+ operability−) {web-api,fullstack-web,distributed,platforms}: Replace a legacy system piece by piece: put a routing layer in front of it, move one capability at a time into the new system, shift traffic over, and retire the old one when nothing routes to it. → `big-ball-of-mud` `shared-database` `facade` `second-system-effect`
- [`circuit-breaker`](entries/circuit-breaker.md) **Circuit Breaker** · pattern/architecture [E] (reliability⊕ runtime+ operability+ delivery−) {distributed,web-api,serverless,platforms} langs:java,cs,ts,py,go,rs: Wrap calls to a remote dependency in an object that counts failures and, past a threshold, fails calls immediately for a while instead of waiting on a service that is down, then lets a trial call through to see whether it has recovered. → `proxy` `fallacies-of-distributed-computing` `state` `murphys-law`
- [`outbox`](entries/outbox.md) **Transactional Outbox** · pattern/architecture [TE] (reliability⊕ operability− runtime−) {distributed,event-driven,web-api} langs:java,cs,py,go: To change your database and publish a message reliably, write the message to an outbox table in the same local transaction as the change, and let a separate relay read the outbox and publish it to the broker. → `shared-database` `saga` `event-sourcing` `cqrs` `fallacies-of-distributed-computing`
- [`saga`](entries/saga.md) **Saga** · pattern/architecture [E] (reliability⊕ delivery− operability−) {distributed,event-driven,serverless} langs:java,cs,go,ts,py: Run a business transaction that spans several services as a sequence of local transactions, each triggering the next, and undo the completed steps with compensating actions if a later step fails. → `outbox` `event-sourcing` `shared-database` `distributed-monolith` `command`
- [`test-double-taxonomy`](entries/test-double-taxonomy.md) **Test Double taxonomy (dummy, stub, spy, mock, fake)** · pattern/testing [E] (change_cost⊕) {web-api,fullstack-web,distributed,event-driven} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: A test double is any stand-in for a real collaborator in a test, and it comes in five kinds that do different jobs. A dummy only fills a parameter. A stub hands back canned answers. A spy records how it was called. A mock checks the calls it gets against expectations. A fake is a working but simplified version, such as an in-memory store. → `mock-everything` `fake-over-mock` `fragile-test` `hard-to-test-code` `contract-test`
- [`golden-master-test`](entries/golden-master-test.md) **Golden Master Test (approval, snapshot or golden-file test)** · pattern/testing [E] (change_cost⊕ delivery+ reliability−) {compilers-tooling,cli-devtool,tui,library-sdk} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Capture the whole output of the code once, have a person check and approve it, store it, and fail the test whenever later output differs. It is the right tool when the output itself is the contract, as with renderers, formatters, compilers, CLI text and serialisers. → `fragile-test` `obscure-test` `erratic-test` `property-based-test`
- [`test-data-builder`](entries/test-data-builder.md) **Test Data Builder** · pattern/testing [E] (change_cost⊕) {web-api,fullstack-web} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Build the objects a test needs through a builder that fills every field with a safe default, so each test sets only the fields that matter to it and reads as what makes the case special. → `obscure-test` `test-code-duplication` `builder` `fluent-interface` `fragile-test`
- [`fluent-interface`](entries/fluent-interface.md) **Fluent Interface** · pattern/design [E] (change_cost⊕ delivery−) {library-sdk} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: An API designed to read like a sentence in the problem's language, usually by chaining calls that each return an object to continue from. Method chaining is the common mechanism, but the aim is readable call sites, not chaining itself. → `builder` `command-query-separation` `message-chains` `law-of-demeter` `test-data-builder`
- [`model-view-update`](entries/model-view-update.md) **Model-View-Update (The Elm Architecture)** · pattern/architecture [E] (change_cost⊕ reliability+ operability+ delivery−) {tui,web-frontend,desktop,mobile} langs:py,ts,cs,go,rs: A UI is one model value, an update function that takes a message and the model and returns the new model plus any commands (effects for the runtime to run), and a view function that renders the model. All change goes through update, and all effects go out as commands. → `functional-core-imperative-shell` `state` `observer` `command` `immutability-by-default` `make-illegal-states-unrepresentable` `ui-thread-confinement` `event-sourcing` `switch-statements`

## Anti-patterns

- [`god-object`](entries/god-object.md) **God object (The Blob)** · anti-pattern/design [AE] (delivery+ change_cost−) {mobile,games,desktop,fullstack-web,web-frontend,tui}: One class holds most of the control and data that should be spread across several, so every change goes through it. Brown et al. call it The Blob; Large Class is the smell it shows up as. → `solid` `facade` `mediator` `large-class` `divergent-change` `interface-bloat` `functional-decomposition`
- [`magic-number`](entries/magic-number.md) **Magic number** · anti-pattern/code [TE] (change_cost−) {embedded,scientific,games,ml-training}: A literal with an important meaning sits in the code with nothing saying what it is, where a named constant should stand. → `primitive-obsession` `principle-of-least-astonishment`
- [`poltergeist`](entries/poltergeist.md) **Poltergeist** · anti-pattern/design [AE] (change_cost−): A class that owns nothing and lives for a moment, made only to kick off work that really belongs to other objects, then thrown away. Close to the Middle Man and Lazy Class smells. → `middle-man` `lazy-class` `command` `adapter` `wrong-abstraction`
- [`interface-bloat`](entries/interface-bloat.md) **Interface bloat (bloated interface)** · anti-pattern/design [E] (delivery+ change_cost−) {library-sdk,plugins-extensions,plugin-host} langs:go: An interface carries so many methods that every client depends on far more than it uses and every implementer must fill in methods it has no use for. The interface segregation principle is the counter-ideal. → `solid` `refused-bequest` `god-object` `speculative-generality` `long-parameter-list` `yagni`
- [`dogma-over-pragma`](entries/dogma-over-pragma.md) **Dogma over pragma** · anti-pattern/design [E] (change_cost− delivery−): A rule or principle is applied because it is the rule, in places where its reason does not hold and it does not make the code better. It differs from cargo cult programming in that the rule is known and named; what is missing is the judgement about when it applies. → `cargo-cult-programming` `wrong-abstraction` `yagni`
- [`business-logic-in-helpers`](entries/business-logic-in-helpers.md) **Business logic in helpers** · anti-pattern/design [AE] (delivery+ change_cost−) {fullstack-web,web-api}: The rules of the domain live in functions in "utils", "helpers" or "common" modules instead of on the domain objects they are about, which are left as bare data. Close to the Anemic Domain Model. → `feature-envy` `drifting-terminology` `functional-decomposition`
- [`drifting-terminology`](entries/drifting-terminology.md) **Drifting terminology** · anti-pattern/design [AE] (change_cost−) {web-api,fullstack-web,platforms,library-sdk}: The same concept goes by different names in different parts of the code, or one name means different things, so the code stops matching how the domain is talked about. DDD's ubiquitous language is the counter-ideal. → `business-logic-in-helpers` `principle-of-least-astonishment`
- [`cargo-cult-programming`](entries/cargo-cult-programming.md) **Cargo cult programming** · anti-pattern/code [AE] (delivery+ change_cost− operability−) {iac,ml-training,serverless}: Code, rituals or structure are copied because they appeared in working code, without understanding what they do or whether they apply here. → `dogma-over-pragma` `copy-and-paste-programming` `lava-flow`
- [`lava-flow`](entries/lava-flow.md) **Lava flow** · anti-pattern/code [ATE] (change_cost−) {ml-training,scientific,data-pipeline}: Dead or half-finished code from earlier experiments hardens into the codebase because nobody knows whether it is still needed and nobody dares remove it. → `dead-code` `boat-anchor` `technical-debt` `cargo-cult-programming`
- [`golden-hammer`](entries/golden-hammer.md) **Golden hammer** · anti-pattern/design [E] (delivery+ change_cost−): One familiar tool, language or technique gets used for every problem, including ones it fits badly. The law of the instrument ("if all you have is a hammer"). → `reinventing-the-wheel` `lindy-effect`
- [`spaghetti-code`](entries/spaghetti-code.md) **Spaghetti code** · anti-pattern/code [E] (delivery+ change_cost−) {scientific,embedded,games}: Control flow is so tangled, with jumps, flags and deep nesting, that you can't follow what happens without tracing it by hand. → `long-method` `big-ball-of-mud` `kiss`
- [`copy-and-paste-programming`](entries/copy-and-paste-programming.md) **Copy-and-paste programming** · anti-pattern/code [ATE] (delivery+ change_cost− reliability−) {iac,data-pipeline,ml-training,web-frontend}: Code is reused by copying it and tweaking the copy, so the same logic lives in several places and a fix in one misses the others. Brown et al. call it Cut-and-Paste Programming; Duplicate Code is the smell. → `dry` `duplicate-code` `shotgun-surgery` `wrong-abstraction` `reinventing-the-wheel`
- [`boat-anchor`](entries/boat-anchor.md) **Boat anchor** · anti-pattern/design [E] (security− change_cost− operability−) {iac,platforms}: A component, library or piece of infrastructure is kept in the system although it serves no purpose, usually because it was costly to get or might be useful later. → `lava-flow` `dead-code` `speculative-generality` `yagni`
- [`reinventing-the-wheel`](entries/reinventing-the-wheel.md) **Reinventing the wheel** · anti-pattern/design [CAE] (security− reliability− change_cost−) {web-api,fullstack-web,scientific}: Writing your own version of something that a standard library, a mature package or the codebase itself already does well, usually with fewer edge cases handled. → `golden-hammer` `copy-and-paste-programming` `duplicate-code`
- [`functional-decomposition`](entries/functional-decomposition.md) **Functional decomposition** · anti-pattern/design [CE] (change_cost−): Procedural code in object-oriented clothing, where classes are named after functions, each holds one routine, and the data travels between them as bare records. → `business-logic-in-helpers` `poltergeist` `god-object` `data-class`
- [`wrong-abstraction`](entries/wrong-abstraction.md) **Wrong abstraction (premature abstraction)** · anti-pattern/design [AE] (delivery+ change_cost−) {web-frontend,library-sdk,iac}: Code that looked alike was merged into one shared abstraction too early, and as the cases diverge it grows parameters and branches until it is harder to change than the duplication was. Sandi Metz's term; Speculative Generality is the related smell. → `dry` `yagni` `speculative-generality` `copy-and-paste-programming` `dogma-over-pragma` `poltergeist`
- [`global-state`](entries/global-state.md) **Global state** · anti-pattern/design [ATE] (delivery+ reliability− change_cost−) {web-api,serverless,web-frontend,ml-training,games,embedded,tui,plugin-host} langs:py,go: Mutable data reachable from anywhere, as global variables, module-level state or singletons, so any code can change it and no caller's behaviour depends only on what it was given. → `singleton` `law-of-demeter`
- [`domain-allergy`](entries/domain-allergy.md) **Domain Allergy** · anti-pattern/architecture [E] (change_cost−) {fullstack-web,web-api,platforms}: Architects and developers treat the business domain as someone else's dull problem and focus on technology, so the system models storage formats or generic "things" instead of the real concepts. → `misapplied-genericity` `over-engineering` `under-modularization` `primitive-obsession`
- [`infrastructure-ignorance`](entries/infrastructure-ignorance.md) **Infrastructure Ignorance** · anti-pattern/architecture (delivery+ reliability− change_cost− runtime− operability−) {embedded,distributed,serverless,mobile}: Designing and building without regard for the environment the system will actually run in (hardware, network, power, security, legal constraints), so it fails requirements in ways that are hard to fix later. → `fallacies-of-distributed-computing` `distributed-monolith` `over-modularization`
- [`misapplied-genericity`](entries/misapplied-genericity.md) **Misapplied Genericity** · anti-pattern/architecture [AE] (change_cost− runtime− operability− delivery−) {library-sdk,platforms,plugins-extensions}: Building a solution for a whole class of problems instead of the one in front of you, so it serves the current case badly and future ones no better. Speculative Generality is the code-scale smell; this is the system-scale version. → `over-engineering` `speculative-generality` `yagni` `domain-allergy` `galls-law`
- [`over-engineering`](entries/over-engineering.md) **Over-Engineering** · anti-pattern/architecture [A] (change_cost− operability− delivery−) {distributed,serverless,iac,platforms}: A system's architecture is more complex than its requirements need, usually through new technology or optimisation for flexibility and scale nobody has asked for. At code scale it overlaps Speculative Generality, which is the canonical name for the class-level form. → `yagni` `premature-optimization` `misapplied-genericity` `domain-allergy` `second-system-effect` `speculative-generality` `kiss`
- [`over-modularization`](entries/over-modularization.md) **Over-Modularization** · anti-pattern/architecture (reliability− change_cost− runtime− operability− delivery−) {distributed,serverless}: Cutting a system into more modules than it needs, at runtime (services, lambdas) or build time (packages, build modules), so the boundaries add more complexity than they remove. Nanoservices is the service-scale name. → `under-modularization` `distributed-monolith` `yagni` `fallacies-of-distributed-computing`
- [`under-modularization`](entries/under-modularization.md) **Under-Modularization** · anti-pattern/architecture (change_cost−) {fullstack-web,web-api,platforms}: Splitting a system into too few modules, so each is too big to understand, secure, deploy or scale, and missing boundaries let unrelated parts depend on each other freely. → `over-modularization` `big-ball-of-mud` `god-object`
- [`shared-database`](entries/shared-database.md) **Shared Database** · anti-pattern/architecture [CE] (operability+ delivery+ reliability− change_cost−) {distributed,platforms,data-pipeline}: Two or more services directly reading and mutating the same tables, so no service owns its data and a schema change or a long transaction in one breaks the others. Also called the integration database. → `distributed-monolith` `over-modularization` `law-of-demeter` `hyrums-law`
- [`big-ball-of-mud`](entries/big-ball-of-mud.md) **Big Ball of Mud** · anti-pattern/architecture [C] (delivery+ change_cost− reliability−) {fullstack-web,web-api,platforms}: A system with no recognisable structure, shaped by expedient fixes, where data and logic are shared freely and every part can reach every other. Malignant Growth is the process that usually produces it; this is the canonical name for the result. → `under-modularization` `technical-debt` `galls-law` `second-system-effect` `lehmans-laws` `broken-windows-theory`
- [`distributed-monolith`](entries/distributed-monolith.md) **Distributed Monolith** · anti-pattern/architecture (reliability− change_cost− runtime− operability− delivery−) {distributed,serverless,event-driven,platforms}: A system split into services that still must be deployed together and fail together, so it carries the costs of distribution without the independence it was supposed to buy. → `over-modularization` `shared-database` `fallacies-of-distributed-computing`
- [`mock-everything`](entries/mock-everything.md) **Mocking Everything (over-mocking)** · anti-pattern/testing [AE] (delivery+ reliability− change_cost−) {web-api,fullstack-web,web-frontend} langs:py,ts,js: A unit test replaces every collaborator of the code under test with a mock, so it only checks that the code calls its mocks the way it was written to, and asserts nothing about real behaviour. Known as over-mocking, and as over-specification or testing implementation details; Meszaros files it under Overspecified Software in Fragile Test. → `fragile-test` `assertion-free-test` `hard-to-test-code` `test-logic-in-production`
- [`assertion-free-test`](entries/assertion-free-test.md) **Assertion-Free Test** · anti-pattern/testing [AE] (delivery+ reliability− change_cost−) {data-pipeline,ml-training,scientific}: A test runs the code but asserts nothing meaningful, so it passes as long as nothing throws. Meszaros's nearest names are Neverfail Test and Manual Result Verification; also called the "secret catcher" or a smoke-only test. → `mock-everything` `manual-intervention` `conditional-test-logic`
- [`anemic-domain-model`](entries/anemic-domain-model.md) **Anemic Domain Model** · anti-pattern/design [CAE] (delivery+ change_cost− reliability−) {web-api,fullstack-web} langs:java,cs,py,ts,go,rs: Domain classes that look like a model (named after business nouns, related to each other) but hold only data, while all the rules live in service classes that read and set their fields. It has the cost of a domain model without its benefit. → `domain-model` `transaction-script` `service-layer` `data-class` `feature-envy` `business-logic-in-helpers` `god-object`
- [`fat-controller`](entries/fat-controller.md) **Fat Controller** · anti-pattern/architecture [AE] (delivery+ change_cost−) {web-api,fullstack-web} langs:py,java,cs,ts,go,rs: Route handlers or controllers that hold the business logic themselves (validation rules, calculations, queries, side effects) instead of parsing the request, calling the application and shaping the response. → `service-layer` `front-controller` `god-object` `long-method` `large-class` `duplicate-code` `transaction-script`
- [`generic-repository`](entries/generic-repository.md) **Generic Repository** · anti-pattern/design [CAE] (change_cost− runtime−) {web-api,fullstack-web} langs:cs,java,ts,py,go: A single Repository<T> with get, get_all, add, update and delete that sits over an ORM which already offers all of that, so it adds a layer without adding meaning and often hides the ORM's useful features. → `repository` `unit-of-work` `misapplied-genericity` `speculative-generality` `middle-man` `over-engineering` `mock-everything`
- [`inner-platform-effect`](entries/inner-platform-effect.md) **Inner-Platform Effect** · anti-pattern/design [E] (change_cost− runtime− operability−) {platforms,fullstack-web,plugin-host}: A system made so configurable that it becomes a poor copy of the platform it runs on: a homemade database inside a database, a scripting language in JSON, a rules engine that only programmers can drive. → `over-engineering` `speculative-generality` `second-system-effect` `reinventing-the-wheel` `misapplied-genericity` `zawinskis-law`
