- [`broken-object-level-authorization`](entries/broken-object-level-authorization.md) **Broken Object Level Authorization (IDOR)** · anti-pattern/security [AE] (security−) {web-api,fullstack-web,mobile,platforms} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go: A handler loads or changes a record by an id the client sent, and checks that the caller is logged in but never that this caller may see or touch that particular record. → `mass-assignment` `trusting-client-input` `least-privilege` `defense-in-depth` `shotgun-surgery`
- [`hard-coded-secrets`](entries/hard-coded-secrets.md) **Hard-coded secrets** · anti-pattern/security [ATE] (delivery+ security− operability−) {iac,serverless,data-pipeline,ml-training,web-api} langs:ts,java,cs,py: Passwords, API keys, tokens or private keys are written into source code, checked-in config or build files, where everyone with the repository, the image or the bundle can read them. → `magic-number` `sensitive-data-in-logs` `least-privilege` `secure-by-default`
- [`injection`](entries/injection.md) **Injection (SQL, command, template)** · anti-pattern/security [AE] (delivery+ security− reliability−) {web-api,fullstack-web,data-pipeline,cli-devtool,databases-storage} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: A query, shell command or template is built by pasting input into a string, so the interpreter can read part of the input as code instead of data. → `validate-at-the-boundary` `trusting-client-input` `least-privilege` `defense-in-depth`
- [`mass-assignment`](entries/mass-assignment.md) **Mass assignment** · anti-pattern/security [ATE] (delivery+ security−) {web-api,fullstack-web,mobile} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: The request body is bound straight onto a domain or database model, so a client can set fields it was never meant to touch (role, owner, price, balance) just by adding them to the request. → `broken-object-level-authorization` `trusting-client-input` `validate-at-the-boundary` `data-class`
- [`sensitive-data-in-logs`](entries/sensitive-data-in-logs.md) **Sensitive data in logs** · anti-pattern/security [ATE] (delivery+ security−) {web-api,distributed,serverless,data-pipeline} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Passwords, tokens, session ids, keys, payment data or personal data are written to logs, traces or error reports, which are kept longer and read by more people and systems than the data was ever meant for. → `hard-coded-secrets` `defense-in-depth` `least-privilege`
- [`user-enumeration`](entries/user-enumeration.md) **User enumeration** · anti-pattern/security [CATE] (security−) {web-api,fullstack-web,mobile} langs:py,java,cs: Login, sign-up or password-reset flows answer differently for unknown and known accounts, in the message, the status code or the time taken, so anyone can find out which emails or usernames have accounts. → `missing-rate-limiting` `defense-in-depth` `secure-by-default`
- [`missing-rate-limiting`](entries/missing-rate-limiting.md) **Missing rate limiting** · anti-pattern/security [AE] (security− reliability−) {web-api,serverless,fullstack-web,platforms} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Endpoints accept as many requests, as large a payload and as big a page as a client cares to send, so one client can guess codes, scrape data, run up a third-party bill or take the service down. → `user-enumeration` `defense-in-depth` `secure-by-default`
- [`ssrf`](entries/ssrf.md) **Server-side request forgery (SSRF)** · anti-pattern/security [TE] (delivery+ security−) {web-api,serverless,platforms,distributed} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: The server fetches a URL the client supplied (a webhook, an image to import, a link preview) without restricting where it may go, so a client can make it call internal services or the cloud metadata endpoint on their behalf. → `secure-by-default` `least-privilege` `defense-in-depth` `validate-at-the-boundary`
- [`insecure-deserialization`](entries/insecure-deserialization.md) **Insecure deserialization** · anti-pattern/security [TE] (delivery+ security−) {distributed,event-driven,ml-training,plugin-host,web-api} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: Data from outside is decoded with a format that can choose which classes to build or which code to run (pickle, Java serialization, BinaryFormatter, polymorphic JSON with type names), so crafted input can run code or build objects the program never meant to. → `validate-at-the-boundary` `trusting-client-input` `defense-in-depth`
- [`trusting-client-input`](entries/trusting-client-input.md) **Trusting client input** · anti-pattern/security [E] (delivery+ security− reliability−) {web-frontend,fullstack-web,mobile,games,web-api} langs:ts,cs,py: A rule is enforced only in the browser, the mobile app or the game client (a validation, a price, a permission, a hidden field), and the server accepts whatever arrives, though anyone can send the request without that client. → `validate-at-the-boundary` `mass-assignment` `broken-object-level-authorization` `defense-in-depth`
- [`swallowed-errors`](entries/swallowed-errors.md) **Swallowed Errors** · anti-pattern/code [ATE] (delivery+ reliability− operability−) {data-pipeline,cli-devtool,web-api,library-sdk,distributed,plugin-host} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: An error is caught or returned and then dropped, so the failure goes on silently and shows up later, somewhere else, as wrong data or a confusing symptom. → `fail-fast` `error-handling-policy` `fail-open-vs-fail-closed` `exceptions-for-control-flow` `murphys-law`
- [`exceptions-for-control-flow`](entries/exceptions-for-control-flow.md) **Exceptions for Control Flow** · anti-pattern/code [E] (delivery+ change_cost− runtime−) {library-sdk,games} langs:py,java,cs,ts,go,rs: Throwing and catching exceptions to steer ordinary, expected logic, such as ending a loop, returning a found value or choosing a branch, instead of using a return value or a condition. → `error-handling-policy` `swallowed-errors` `principle-of-least-astonishment`
- [`inconsistent-error-contract`](entries/inconsistent-error-contract.md) **Inconsistent Error Contract** · anti-pattern/api [AE] (delivery+ reliability− change_cost− operability−) {web-api,fullstack-web,cli-devtool,platforms,serverless} langs:py,java,cs,ts,go: Endpoints or commands of one API report failure in different ways, with different status codes, body shapes, field names or exit codes for the same kind of error, so clients have to special-case each one. → `error-handling-policy` `breaking-change-surface` `drifting-terminology` `principle-of-least-astonishment` `hyrums-law`
- [`resource-leak`](entries/resource-leak.md) **Resource Leak** · anti-pattern/code [TE] (delivery+ reliability− runtime−) {web-api,distributed,databases-storage,tui,desktop,embedded} langs:go,rs,py,java,cs,ts: Something acquired, such as a file, socket, connection, response body, lock, goroutine or background task, is not released on every path, especially the error path, so the process slowly runs out of it. → `swallowed-errors` `murphys-law` `init-time-side-effects`
- [`init-time-side-effects`](entries/init-time-side-effects.md) **Init-Time Side Effects** · anti-pattern/design [ATE] (delivery+ reliability− change_cost− runtime− operability−) {cli-devtool,library-sdk,serverless,plugin-host,plugins-extensions} langs:go,py,java,cs,ts,rs: Real work, such as reading config or env, opening connections, registering global state or making network calls, runs when a module is imported or a package initialised, before the program's entry point has had a say. → `global-state` `singleton` `hard-to-test-code` `fail-fast`
- [`terminal-escape-injection`](entries/terminal-escape-injection.md) **Terminal escape injection** · anti-pattern/security [E] (security−) {cli-devtool,tui,compilers-tooling,plugin-host} langs:py,ts,go,rs: A program writes text it doesn't control (file names, remote data, commit messages, log lines) straight to a terminal, so escape and control sequences in that text are run by the terminal: they can hide or fake output, retitle the window, write the clipboard, or in older terminals make the terminal type commands back. → `injection` `sensitive-data-in-logs` `validate-at-the-boundary` `trusting-client-input` `defense-in-depth`
- [`patch-where-looked-up`](entries/patch-where-looked-up.md) **Patching where defined, not where looked up** · anti-pattern/testing [AE] (reliability− change_cost−) {web-api,cli-devtool,data-pipeline,fullstack-web} langs:py,ts,java,cs,go,rs: A test patches or mocks a name in the module that defines it, but the code under test looks the name up somewhere else (its own import, a captured reference), so the patch never takes effect and the real code runs. → `mock-everything` `test-double-taxonomy` `hard-to-test-code` `global-state` `init-time-side-effects` `dependency-injection` `assertion-free-test`
- [`overloaded-environment-flag`](entries/overloaded-environment-flag.md) **Overloaded environment flag** · anti-pattern/security [ATE] (delivery+ security− operability−) {web-api,fullstack-web,serverless,platforms} langs:py,ts,java,cs: One environment flag (DEBUG, a dev, local or test mode) switches on several unrelated risky behaviours at once, such as detailed error pages, skipped auth, open CORS, weak secret checks or a fake payment provider, so turning it on for one reason turns on all of them, and one leaked setting opens them all. → `secure-by-default` `test-logic-in-production` `fail-open-vs-fail-closed` `least-privilege` `hard-coded-secrets` `global-state` `shotgun-surgery`

## Smells

- [`obscure-test`](entries/obscure-test.md) **Obscure Test** · smell/testing [E] (delivery+ change_cost−): You can't tell at a glance what behaviour a test checks, either because it hides what matters (Mystery Guest) or buries it under detail (Eager Test, General Fixture, Irrelevant Information, Hard-Coded Test Data, Indirect Testing). Also called Long Test, Complex Test or Verbose Test. → `assertion-roulette` `test-code-duplication`
- [`conditional-test-logic`](entries/conditional-test-logic.md) **Conditional Test Logic** · smell/testing [ATE] (reliability− change_cost−) langs:go: A test contains branches or loops, so you can't be sure which path runs or whether it checks anything at all. Also called Indented Test Code; its causes include Flexible Test, Conditional Verification Logic, Production Logic in Test and Complex Teardown. → `obscure-test` `erratic-test` `assertion-free-test`
- [`hard-to-test-code`](entries/hard-to-test-code.md) **Hard-to-Test Code** · smell/testing [E] (delivery+ change_cost− reliability−) {embedded,games,desktop,mobile,serverless,event-driven,tui}: The code resists being tested in isolation because it is tightly coupled, asynchronous, hides what a test needs to reach, or can't be constructed without half the system. → `singleton` `test-logic-in-production` `mock-everything` `fragile-test`
- [`test-code-duplication`](entries/test-code-duplication.md) **Test Code Duplication** · smell/testing [CAE] (delivery+ change_cost−): The same setup, exercise or verification code is copied across many tests, so one change to the code under test means editing them all. Usually Cut-and-Paste Code Reuse or Reinventing the Wheel. → `duplicate-code` `obscure-test`
- [`test-logic-in-production`](entries/test-logic-in-production.md) **Test Logic in Production** · smell/testing [ATE] (delivery+ reliability− security−) {web-api,fullstack-web,serverless,platforms} langs:rs,go: Production code contains logic that exists only for tests, such as a Test Hook that switches behaviour when testing, methods For Tests Only, a dependency on test code, or Equality Pollution. → `hard-to-test-code` `mock-everything`
- [`assertion-roulette`](entries/assertion-roulette.md) **Assertion Roulette** · smell/testing [CE] (change_cost−): A test has several assertions and when it fails you can't tell which one, usually because it is an Eager Test or the assertions have no messages. → `obscure-test` `frequent-debugging`
- [`erratic-test`](entries/erratic-test.md) **Erratic Test** · smell/testing [TE] (reliability− change_cost− delivery−) {distributed,event-driven,web-frontend,mobile,databases-storage,tui}: A test passes sometimes and fails other times with no code change, today usually called a flaky test. Causes include Interacting Tests, Test Run War, Unrepeatable Test, Resource Leakage, Resource Optimism and Nondeterministic Test. → `slow-tests` `fragile-test` `hard-to-test-code` `conditional-test-logic`
- [`fragile-test`](entries/fragile-test.md) **Fragile Test** · smell/testing [E] (delivery+ change_cost−) {web-frontend,fullstack-web,compilers-tooling,cli-devtool,tui}: Tests break when the code changes in ways that don't affect what they're testing, through one of four sensitivities (interface, behaviour, data, context), Overspecified Software, Sensitive Equality or a Fragile Fixture. → `mock-everything` `obscure-test` `hard-to-test-code`
- [`frequent-debugging`](entries/frequent-debugging.md) **Frequent Debugging** · smell/testing (change_cost−) {distributed,embedded}: Most test failures need a debugger or print statements to find the cause, because the suite lacks defect localization. Also called Manual Debugging. → `assertion-roulette` `slow-tests`
- [`manual-intervention`](entries/manual-intervention.md) **Manual Intervention** · smell/testing [TE] (change_cost− reliability−) {embedded,mobile,desktop,games,iac}: A test needs a person to do something each run, whether setting up the environment, injecting an event or checking the result by eye. → `assertion-free-test` `slow-tests`
- [`slow-tests`](entries/slow-tests.md) **Slow Tests** · smell/testing [TE] (change_cost− delivery−) {fullstack-web,databases-storage,data-pipeline,ml-training}: The tests take so long that people stop running them on every change. Causes include Slow Component Usage (usually the database), a General Fixture, Asynchronous Test and Too Many Tests. → `erratic-test` `frequent-debugging` `hard-to-test-code`
- [`alternative-classes-with-different-interfaces`](entries/alternative-classes-with-different-interfaces.md) **Alternative Classes with Different Interfaces** · smell/design [AE] (delivery+ change_cost−) {library-sdk,platforms}: Two classes do the same job behind different method names and signatures, so callers can't swap one for the other and nobody notices they are duplicates. → `duplicate-code` `adapter` `dry` `wrong-abstraction`
- [`comments`](entries/comments.md) **Comments** · smell/code [CAE] (delivery+ change_cost−): A method needs comments to explain what its code does, which usually means the code itself could be clearer. Fowler calls such comments a deodorant. → `long-method` `kiss`
- [`data-class`](entries/data-class.md) **Data Class** · smell/design [CE] (delivery+ change_cost−) {fullstack-web,web-api} langs:py,java: A class holds only fields and accessors, while the logic that works on that data lives in the classes that use it. → `feature-envy`
- [`data-clumps`](entries/data-clumps.md) **Data Clumps** · smell/code [TE] (delivery+ change_cost− reliability−) {scientific,games}: The same few values travel together through fields and parameter lists in several places, which says they are one concept that has no name yet. → `long-parameter-list` `primitive-obsession`
- [`dead-code`](entries/dead-code.md) **Dead Code** · smell/code [ATE] (delivery+ change_cost−) {library-sdk,plugins-extensions}: Code that nothing runs or uses any more: variables, parameters, branches, functions, classes or whole files left behind after requirements changed. → `speculative-generality` `yagni` `boy-scout-rule`
- [`divergent-change`](entries/divergent-change.md) **Divergent Change** · smell/code [E] (delivery+ change_cost−) {fullstack-web,web-api}: One class keeps getting edited for unrelated reasons, so changes about different concerns all land in the same place. It is the mirror image of Shotgun Surgery. → `shotgun-surgery` `large-class` `solid` `god-object`
- [`duplicate-code`](entries/duplicate-code.md) **Duplicate Code** · smell/code [ATE] (delivery+ change_cost− reliability−) {iac,data-pipeline,scientific,web-frontend}: The same logic appears in more than one place, so every fix or change has to be made in each copy and the copies drift. Fowler calls it Duplicated Code. → `dry` `wrong-abstraction` `alternative-classes-with-different-interfaces` `shotgun-surgery`
- [`feature-envy`](entries/feature-envy.md) **Feature Envy** · smell/design [E] (delivery+ change_cost−) {fullstack-web,web-api}: A method uses another object's data more than its own, which suggests it lives in the wrong class. → `data-class` `law-of-demeter` `strategy` `visitor` `inappropriate-intimacy`
- [`inappropriate-intimacy`](entries/inappropriate-intimacy.md) **Inappropriate Intimacy** · smell/design [TE] (delivery+ change_cost− reliability−) {library-sdk,plugins-extensions,plugin-host} langs:py: Two classes reach into each other's private fields and methods, so neither can change without the other. Inappropriate Intimacy is the name most developers know, and Insider Trading is the current one. → `feature-envy` `message-chains` `law-of-demeter`
- [`incomplete-library-class`](entries/incomplete-library-class.md) **Incomplete Library Class** · smell/design [TE] (delivery+ change_cost−) {library-sdk,plugins-extensions} langs:cs,rs,py: A library you depend on is missing something you need and you can't change its source, so the extra behaviour ends up scattered across callers. → `adapter` `decorator` `facade`
- [`large-class`](entries/large-class.md) **Large Class** · smell/code [ATE] (delivery+ change_cost−) {fullstack-web,desktop,mobile,games}: A class has grown too many fields, methods or lines because new features kept landing there. Taken to the extreme it becomes a God Object. → `god-object` `divergent-change` `long-method` `solid`
- [`lazy-class`](entries/lazy-class.md) **Lazy Class** · smell/design [E] (change_cost−): A class does too little to be worth understanding and maintaining. → `speculative-generality` `middle-man` `primitive-obsession` `yagni`
- [`long-method`](entries/long-method.md) **Long Method** · smell/code [CATE] (delivery+ change_cost−) {data-pipeline,scientific,ml-training,compilers-tooling,tui}: A function has grown long enough that you have to read all of it to understand any of it. → `comments` `large-class` `kiss` `duplicate-code`
- [`long-parameter-list`](entries/long-parameter-list.md) **Long Parameter List** · smell/code [ATE] (delivery+ change_cost− reliability−) {scientific,ml-training,library-sdk} langs:py: A function takes so many parameters that calls are hard to read and easy to get wrong. → `data-clumps` `primitive-obsession` `builder`
- [`message-chains`](entries/message-chains.md) **Message Chains** · smell/design [TE] (delivery+ change_cost−): A client walks a chain of objects to reach the one it wants, so it depends on the whole path between them. This is what the Law of Demeter forbids. → `law-of-demeter` `middle-man` `inappropriate-intimacy`
- [`middle-man`](entries/middle-man.md) **Middle Man** · smell/design [AE] (change_cost−) {library-sdk}: A class mostly forwards calls to another class and adds nothing of its own. → `message-chains` `lazy-class` `proxy` `decorator` `facade` `adapter`
- [`parallel-inheritance-hierarchies`](entries/parallel-inheritance-hierarchies.md) **Parallel Inheritance Hierarchies** · smell/design [E] (change_cost−) {compilers-tooling,desktop}: Every time you add a subclass in one hierarchy you have to add a matching subclass in another. → `shotgun-surgery` `divergent-change` `visitor` `bridge`
- [`primitive-obsession`](entries/primitive-obsession.md) **Primitive Obsession** · smell/code [ATE] (delivery+ change_cost− reliability− security−) {web-api,platforms,fullstack-web,databases-storage} langs:py,ts,rs,go: Domain concepts such as money, ranges, ids, phone numbers and statuses are passed around as bare strings and numbers, so their rules are repeated wherever they are used. → `data-clumps` `long-parameter-list` `switch-statements` `lazy-class`
- [`refused-bequest`](entries/refused-bequest.md) **Refused Bequest** · smell/design [TE] (delivery+ reliability− change_cost−) {library-sdk,plugins-extensions,desktop} langs:java: A subclass inherits methods and fields it doesn't want, ignoring them or overriding them to throw, which means the inheritance was chosen for code reuse rather than because the subclass really is a kind of its parent. → `parallel-inheritance-hierarchies`
- [`shotgun-surgery`](entries/shotgun-surgery.md) **Shotgun Surgery** · smell/design [AE] (change_cost− reliability−) {web-api,fullstack-web,platforms,distributed}: One change forces many small edits across many classes or files, because one responsibility is spread across them. It is the mirror image of Divergent Change, and it is easy to miss on a file-by-file read since it only shows across files and history. → `divergent-change` `duplicate-code` `parallel-inheritance-hierarchies` `dry` `solid` `switch-statements`
- [`speculative-generality`](entries/speculative-generality.md) **Speculative Generality** · smell/design [AE] (change_cost− delivery−) {library-sdk,plugins-extensions,platforms,cli-devtool,plugin-host}: Hooks, parameters, abstract classes and extension points were added for needs that might come someday and never did. It is YAGNI seen in the code. → `yagni` `dead-code` `lazy-class` `kiss` `second-system-effect`
- [`switch-statements`](entries/switch-statements.md) **Switch Statements** · smell/code [CATE] (delivery+ change_cost− reliability−) {compilers-tooling,platforms,tui} langs:rs,ts: A switch or if-else chain on the same type code shows up in several places, so adding a case means finding and editing every copy. → `strategy` `state` `primitive-obsession` `shotgun-surgery` `factory-method`
- [`temporary-field`](entries/temporary-field.md) **Temporary Field** · smell/code [TE] (delivery+ change_cost− reliability−): Some of an object's fields hold values only while one algorithm runs and are empty the rest of the time, which confuses anyone reading the class. → `long-parameter-list` `long-method` `state`
- [`n-plus-one-queries`](entries/n-plus-one-queries.md) **N+1 Queries** · smell/code [AE] (delivery+ runtime−) {web-api,fullstack-web,databases-storage} langs:py,java,cs,ts,go,rs: Code fetches a list with one query and then runs one more query per item to load something related, so a page of 100 rows costs 101 round trips; usually hidden by an ORM's lazy loading. → `premature-optimization` `law-of-leaky-abstractions` `table-data-gateway` `repository` `data-mapper`
- [`validation-drift`](entries/validation-drift.md) **Validation drift** · smell/design [AE] (delivery+ reliability− security− change_cost−) {fullstack-web,web-frontend,mobile,web-api} langs:py,ts,java,cs: The same input rules are written separately in the front end and the back end (or in a client and a server, or two services), and the copies drift apart, so the form accepts what the API rejects or the API accepts what the form never would. → `trusting-client-input` `validate-at-the-boundary` `duplicate-code` `dry` `shotgun-surgery` `parse-dont-validate`
- [`variant-drift`](entries/variant-drift.md) **Variant drift (parallel implementations out of step)** · smell/design [AE] (delivery+ reliability− change_cost−) {databases-storage,mobile,desktop,platforms,fullstack-web} langs:py,ts,go,rs,java,cs: Several implementations of the same thing that must change together, such as one query module per database dialect, one renderer per platform or one code path per product edition, and a change made to one variant alone leaves the others behind. → `shotgun-surgery` `parallel-inheritance-hierarchies` `contract-test` `duplicate-code` `dry` `liskov-substitution-principle` `strategy`
